summary: Introductory intake for vendor onboarding focused on data deletion rights (DDR), KMS/HSM key management handoff options, and approval path for MSA/DPA and SLA tiers. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted with emphasis on EU data residency and HSM-backed keys.
topics: KMS / HSM options and key custody
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-25 14:30 UTC — Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (CSM), Jordan (Nexera - Procurement), Aisha (InfoSec), Tom (Cloud Architect), Renee (Legal)

Summary: short intake call to map vendor acceptance pathway, discuss MSA/DPA redlines and KMS handoff, plus data deletion SLA (DDR) expectations.

00:00 Jordan (Nexera): Okay thanks everyone for making time, we wanted to use this session to make sure the legal and security asks are mapped out for vendor onboarding. We have a procurement window in early December but legal needs the MSA redlines and a clear KMS plan.
00:27 Priya (Redwood AE): Thanks Jordan, totally. Hi all — Priya from Redwood. I'll run through the high-level path and Liam will jump in on the technical KMS and Dedicated options. We do have a security pack and SOC2 artifacts, I'll share links after.
00:45 Aisha (InfoSec): Quick ask up front — we need to ensure data residency for EU workflows and we require HSM-backed key custody for any patient-identifiable processing, also clear DDR steps.
01:05 Liam (SE): Yep, understood. We support three deployment patterns that map to those asks: Hosted API with tenant-level encryption, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in customer VPC), and Private (on-prem or VPC with a customer-controlled control plane). For HSM/KMS — we can integrate with your cloud KMS or sync with an HSM via our private connector. There's a couple of patterns.
01:34 Tom (Cloud): When you say "sync with HSM" is that a key export or do you keep key material? Our policy forbids third-party key export.
01:45 Liam (SE): We never require key export. Option A: customer-managed keys in their KMS with envelope encryption — Redwood holds only the wrapped keys needed at runtime but can't unwrap without access to your KMS. Option B: HSM-backed signing for token ops and ephemeral keys — in that case the key material never leaves your HSM, we call out for a PKCS interface or a cloud HSM endpoint. Some customers refer to this as a "KMS handoff".
02:12 Renee (Legal): For MSA/DPA redlines — our counsel will want an explicit clause about DDR latency: a guaranteed process to remove customer data from caches and backups and confirmation within X days. Do you have standard DDR language?
02:30 Priya: We do, yes. Our standard DPA has a DDR clause with a 30-day confirmation for hosted artifacts and a 14-day SLA for Dedicated because we can control wipe job scheduling. We can surface an enterprise tweak to 7 days with an HSM + no-logs mode if that's required — need to confirm internally but we've done that with other regulated customers.
03:05 Aisha: 14 days still a bit long for us for PHI, we usually ask for 7. Also need audit logs that show deletion events and proof of key revocation.
03:20 Maya (CSM): We can attach audit export — token-level events and deletion confirmations. We log KMS operations but some of the event names in our current logging are abbreviated, note there might be transcription mismatch in artifact names like K-V cache being logged as KV cash in older versions.
03:45 Jordan: Pricing will matter — procurement needs to see the delta between Hosted and Dedicated, also any egress or cross-region fees. We typically prefer reserved for cost predictability.
04:02 Liam: For the typical LLM workload you described in the intake form (short chat interactions, 256 tokens average, bursty traffic during business hours), Dedicated with a 12-month commit is usually ~30-40% cheaper on per-token basis after you amortize GPU reservation. We'll sketch a short comparison.
04:28 Tom: And for latency — will Dedicated give us a stricter SLO? We need 95th percentile under 200ms for short prompts, or we can't use it for the triage layer.
04:42 Liam: Depends on model family and quantization. We can target 95th <200ms with a mid-size open model and optimized kernels on Dedicated; with Hosted we can hit sub-200ms on certain model variants but can't guarantee during heavy multi-tenant spikes, hence the SLA tiering.
05:10 Renee: Are you SOC 2 Type II and do you have an attestation we can share? Also any pen test reports?
05:20 Priya: Yes SOC 2 Type II — will share the report link. We also have red-team summaries and can provide a pen test attestation under NDA.
05:34 Aisha: How do you handle log retention? We need log retention choices per dataset and the ability to opt out of telemetry.
05:45 Liam: You can configure retention per route. For Dedicated and Private you can set zero-retention for specific endpoints and leverage prefix caching off; but note this impacts features like context-aware caching and performance improvements. We'll document tradeoffs.
06:10 Jordan: Back to legal — if we sign MSA with exceptions, what's the typical turnaround to finalize DPA + SLA? Our window is mid-November final sign-off.
06:25 Priya: If we get a prioritized redline list this week, Legal + Solutions can often ship a counter-redline in 5 business days. Then it's mostly negotiation. For enterprise tweaks like 7-day DDR or HSM integration we'd need a short SOW addendum but can align within your timeline.
06:50 Tom: About KMS: does Redwood support bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) for both AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS?
07:00 Liam: Yes, we support both AWS KMS and GCP KMS, and we've integrated with YubiHSM and Azure Key Vault for other customers. For HSM on-prem we use a PKCS#11 interface or an HTTPS gateway depending on the customer's environment.
07:25 Aisha: We need an example architecture diagram where the key material is never persisted on Redwood hosts and a sequence diagram for a deletion.
07:40 Liam: We'll attach a diagram — we've done a schematic for a customer previously where key ops go through a proxy that signs ephemeral session keys; we can reuse that and anonymize it.
08:00 Jordan: Any vendor scoring concerns? Our security team runs a third-party vendor questionnaire — can you support SSP answers and provide a contact for fill-in?
08:15 Maya: Yes, we have an SSP template and a dedicated security contact. We'll provide that contact info and a filled example.
08:30 Renee: On indemnity and liability caps — we may need to negotiate SLA credits for data incidents and retention failures.
08:40 Priya: Typical approach: SLA credits tied to availability and data-handling lapses, and we can define specific remedies in the SOW. We'll flag that to Legal.
08:55 Jordan: Can you outline a minimal acceptance test for procurement — like functional + security checks before we flip production?
09:10 Liam: Minimal acceptance: 1) Test calls to the hosted endpoint verifying encryption in transit and at rest, 2) DDR test: create sample data, request deletion, confirm logs and key rotation, 3) Latency/load test: 1k requests over 10 minutes to validate 95th pctl SLO, 4) KMS handshake verification. We'll put a checklist in the follow-up.
09:42 Aisha: For DDR test we want an auditable confirmation and signed attestation — can you provide a deletion certificate?
09:55 Maya: We provide deletion confirmations with a signed digest and timestamp; for Dedicated we can include a low-level wipe job log that references the shard IDs.
10:15 Priya: Quick pause — I want to note links we'll share: Security Pack: https://drive.redwood/security/nexera-pack ; MSA redline template: https://redwood.app/legal/msaredline ; KMS arch diagram: https://redwood.app/arch/kms-handbook (these are placeholders, we'll include proper links in follow-up).
10:40 Jordan: Good, thank you. On pricing approvals — who at Redwood will own the pricing exception?
10:50 Priya: I'll own the pricing path and coordinate with finance — Liam will produce the cost modeling, Maya will help surface any credits for longer commit.
11:05 Tom: One more technical detail — you mentioned KV cache and prefix caching affecting DDR, how is cached content treated for deletion?
11:18 Liam: Good question. Our cache is a combination of in-memory KV for short lived prefixes and optional persistent cache for performance. For DDR we purge the in-memory KV immediately and schedule persistent cache wipe within the DDR SLA window; on Dedicated we can do near-immediate expunge. We'll document the exact TTLs per deployment.
11:45 Renee: We may ask for a change to the DPA that includes a guarantee of key revocation notification.
11:55 Priya: Noted. We can add an outbound webhook or email notification for key revocation events as part of the enterprise DPA.
12:10 Jordan: Timeline wise — if we get the redlines next 48 hours can we target final sign by mid-November?
12:20 Priya: Yes, that aligns. We'll aim to get draft redlines and the tech checklist to you within 48 hours.
12:35 Aisha: Okay, looks good. We'll compile our legal exceptions and send them with any SOC2 follow-ups.
12:48 Priya: Great — recap: we'll send MSA/DPA redline, security pack, cost sketch, KMS architectural diagram, and acceptance checklist. Follow-up call w/ engineering to deep-dive KMS and pen test artifacts week of Nov 8.
12:59 Jordan: Thanks all.
13:05 Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript includes a few colloquial transcriptions: e.g., "K-V cash" instead of "KV cache" in some auto-generated snippets; names and acronyms spelled inconsistently. Shared artifacts referenced and to be attached in follow-up: security pack, MSA redline, KMS diagrams, cost sketch.
